---
title: "Searching the reports with ragnar"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(contoso)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## Introduction

This article loads the [business reports](business-reports.qmd) into a
[ragnar](https://ragnar.tidyverse.org) store: a single 'DuckDB' file you can
search by keyword, filter by report metadata, query with SQL, and hand to an
LLM as context.

The store uses BM25 keyword search only. There are no embeddings, so you need
no embedding model, provider or API key to build or search it.

The one design rule: **every chunk carries all of its report's metadata as
typed columns.** That is what lets you filter by publication date, unit or
report type inside the database, and cite the source of every hit.

You need these packages:

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false
install.packages(c("ragnar", "dplyr", "purrr", "DBI"))
```

## Step 1: read the reports

`read_reports()` returns one row per report: eight metadata columns (the
dates already as `Date`) and a `body` column with the Markdown text.

```{r}
#| label: read-reports
reports <- read_reports()


dplyr::glimpse(reports |> select(-body))
```

## Step 2: create an empty store

`embed = NULL` turns off embeddings. `extra_cols` declares the metadata
columns that every chunk will carry, with their types. Passing zero rows of
the reports table declares exactly the columns and types above.

```{r}
#| label: create-store
#| message: false
store_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".duckdb")

meta_cols <- c(
  "id",
  "title",
  "unit",
  "author",
  "report_type",
  "period_start",
  "period_end",
  "published"
)
report_store <- ragnar::ragnar_store_create(
  store_path,
  embed = NULL,
  extra_cols = reports[0, meta_cols]
)
```

Use a real path such as `"reports.duckdb"` instead of `tempfile()` to keep the
store between sessions.

## Step 3: chunk one report and attach its metadata

ragnar splits a document into overlapping chunks of about 1,600 characters.
Each chunk records where it starts and ends in the body, and the headings
above it (`context`). Chunk the `body` text, and set `origin` to the report
`id` so every chunk links back to its report.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-one-report

report <- reports |>
  dplyr::filter(id == "ecommerce-2025-06")

chunks <-
  report$body |>
  ragnar::MarkdownDocument(origin = report$id) |>
  ragnar::markdown_chunk()
```

To browse the chunks with each one rendered as Markdown, open ragnar's
viewer. It is a Shiny app, so run it in your own session:

```{r}
#| label: view-chunks
#| eval: false
chunks |>
  ragnar::ragnar_chunks_view()
```

The chunks know nothing about the report yet. Pulling in the metadata is one
`mutate()`: every metadata value is a single value, so it is repeated on each
chunk.

```{r}
#| label: attach-metadata

chunks <-
  chunks |>
  cross_join(report |> select(-body))

chunks |>
  dplyr::select(start, end, id, unit, report_type, published)
```

## Step 4: insert every report

Repeat step 3 for each report and insert the chunks into the store.
`pwalk()` passes `body` by name and the eight metadata columns through
`...`.

```{r}
#| label: insert-reports

insert_report <- function(report) {
  ragnar::MarkdownDocument(report$body, origin = report$id) |>
    ragnar::markdown_chunk() |>
    dplyr::cross_join(dplyr::select(report, -body)) |>
    ragnar::ragnar_store_insert(report_store, chunks = _)
}


reports |>
  dplyr::group_split(id) |>
  purrr::walk(insert_report, .progress = TRUE)
```

### Or: start from exported files

If you work from the files written by `export_reports()`, read each YAML file
with `yaml12::read_yaml()`. It returns the metadata and the body together, so
the rest is the same. Convert the dates back to `Date`, because YAML stores
them as text. Do not point `ragnar::read_as_markdown()` at the YAML files:
it would chunk the raw YAML, keys and all.

```{r}
#| label: insert-from-files
#| eval: false
paths <- export_reports("contoso-reports")

reports <- paths |>
  purrr::map(\(path) tibble::as_tibble(yaml12::read_yaml(path))) |>
  purrr::list_rbind() |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(period_start, period_end, published), as.Date))
```

## Step 5: build the search index

This builds the 'DuckDB' full-text (BM25) index over the chunk text and
headings. Run it after every insert.

```{r}
#| label: build-index
ragnar::ragnar_store_build_index(report_store)
```

Check the result: every report has chunks and no metadata is missing.

```{r}
#| label: check-store
DBI::dbGetQuery(
  report_store@con,
  "
  select count(distinct id) as reports,
         count(*) as n
  from chunks"
)
```

## Step 6: search

`ragnar_retrieve_bm25()` returns one row per matching chunk, with all of the
metadata columns attached.

```{r}
#| label: search
hits <- ragnar::ragnar_retrieve_bm25(
  report_store,
  "ShopSphere marketplace",
  top_k = 5
)

hits |>
  dplyr::select(id, unit, published, chunk_id, metric_value)
```

How to read a row:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | The excerpt itself, about 1,600 characters |
| `id`, `title`, `unit`, `author`, `report_type` | Which report it came from |
| `period_start`, `period_end` | The period the report covers |
| `published` | When the report was released |
| `chunk_id`, `start`, `end` | Which excerpt of the report, and where it sits in the body |
| `context` | The headings above the excerpt |
| `metric_value` | BM25 score. Higher is a better match. Only comparable within one search |

Chunks overlap by about half, so two neighbouring chunks of the same report
can both appear. Treat them as one source.

## Step 7: use the store from an LLM

Wrap the search in a function that always applies the `as_of` filter, and
register it as an 'ellmer' tool. Return JSON from the tool rather than a data
frame. This needs an API key, so it is not run here.

```{r}
#| label: llm-tool
#| eval: false
search_reports <- function(query, as_of, top_k = 6) {
  ragnar::ragnar_retrieve_bm25(
    report_store,
    query,
    top_k = top_k,
    filter = published <= as.Date(as_of)
  ) |>
    dplyr::select(id, title, unit, author, published, context, text) |>
    jsonlite::toJSON(Date = "ISO8601")
}


chat <- ellmer::chat_anthropic(
  system_prompt = "Answer using the search_reports tool. Today is 2025-06-30;
    always pass as_of = '2025-06-30'. Cite report ids."
)

chat$register_tool(ellmer::tool(
  search_reports,
  description = "Keyword (BM25) search over Contoso business-unit reports.
    Not semantic: try two or three phrasings using the reports' own terms.",
  arguments = list(
    query = ellmer::type_string("Keywords."),
    as_of = ellmer::type_string(
      "YYYY-MM-DD. Only reports published on or before this date."
    ),
    top_k = ellmer::type_integer("Maximum number of hits.", required = FALSE)
  ),
  name = "search_reports"
))

chat$chat("Why is online revenue below plan this year?")
```

`ragnar::ragnar_register_tool_retrieve()` and `ragnar::mcp_serve_store()` do
this in one line, but they cannot apply an `as_of` filter, so the model can
read later reports.

```{r}
#| label: cleanup
#| include: false
DBI::dbDisconnect(report_store@con)
unlink(store_path)
```

## Use the reports from an assistant

These examples need an API key or an assistant, so they are not run here.

### Posit Assistant, with a date filter

Save the store to a fixed path, such as `~/ragnar/contoso-reports.duckdb`,
then save this script as `~/ragnar/serve_reports.R`. It serves one search
tool over MCP. `as_of` is required and `from` is optional, so the assistant
can narrow a search to a period but can never read reports published after
`as_of`.

```{r}
#| label: serve-reports
#| eval: false
report_store <- ragnar::ragnar_store_connect(
  Sys.getenv("REPORTS_STORE"),
  read_only = TRUE
)

search_reports <- function(
  query,
  to_date,
  from_date = "1900-01-01",
  top_k = 6
) {
  ragnar::ragnar_retrieve_bm25(
    report_store,
    query,
    top_k = top_k,
    filter = published >= as.Date(from_date) & published <= as.Date(to_date)
  ) |>
    dplyr::select(id, title, unit, author, published, text) |>
    jsonlite::toJSON(Date = "ISO8601")
}

search_tool <- ellmer::tool(
  search_reports,
  name = "search_reports",
  description = "Keyword (BM25) search over Contoso's 2016-2025 internal business reports.
    Only reports published on or before `as_of` are searched.",
  arguments = list(
    query = ellmer::type_string("Keywords to search for."),
    to_date = ellmer::type_string(
      "Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Only reports published on or before this date are searched."
    ),
    from_date = ellmer::type_string(
      "Optional start date, YYYY-MM-DD. Only reports published on or after this date are searched.",
      required = FALSE
    ),
    top_k = ellmer::type_integer(
      "Number of excerpts to return. Default 6.",
      required = FALSE
    )
  )
)

mcptools::mcp_server(list(search_tool), session_tools = FALSE)
```

Then add the server to `~/.posit/assistant/settings.json` and reload:

```json
"mcpServers": {
  "contoso-reports": {
    "type": "local",
    "command": ["Rscript", "/home/you/ragnar/serve_reports.R"],
    "environment": {
      "REPORTS_STORE": "/home/you/ragnar/contoso-reports.duckdb"
    },
    "timeout": 60000
  }
}
```

### commons

[commons](https://posit-dev.github.io/commons/) builds an agent that labels
each answer by where it came from. Give it the same date-filtered search as a
**measure**, a trusted function the agent calls with arguments, so its
answers come from the ragnar store and are labelled Trusted. commons also
needs a data source; the report metadata (no text) works, so the agent can
answer questions such as "which reports came out in June?" with SQL.

Leave out commons' `context_layer()`: its own search over the report text
cannot filter by date, so it would give the agent a way around `as_of`.

commons does not list measures in its prompt; the agent has to look them up
first. Without `instructions` pointing it to `search_reports`, it tends to
query the metadata table, find no text, and give up.

```{r}
#| label: commons-agent
#| eval: false

report_store <- ragnar::ragnar_store_connect(
  Sys.getenv("REPORTS_STORE"),
  read_only = TRUE
)

search_reports <- function(query, as_of, from = "1900-01-01", top_k = 6) {
  ragnar::ragnar_retrieve_bm25(
    report_store,
    query,
    top_k = top_k,
    filter = published >= !!as.Date(from) & published <= !!as.Date(as_of)
  ) |>
    dplyr::select(id, title, unit, author, published, text) |>
    jsonlite::toJSON(Date = "ISO8601")
}

search_measure <- commons::measure(
  "search_reports",
  "Search the text of Contoso's 2016-2025 business reports (what business units wrote and said). Only reports published on or before as_of are searched.",
  fn = search_reports,
  arguments = list(
    query = ellmer::type_string("Keywords to search for."),
    as_of = ellmer::type_string("Date as YYYY-MM-DD."),
    from = ellmer::type_string(
      "Optional start date, YYYY-MM-DD.",
      required = FALSE
    ),
    top_k = ellmer::type_integer(
      "Number of excerpts. Default 6.",
      required = FALSE
    )
  )
)

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "reports", dplyr::select(read_reports(), -body))

agent <- commons::commons(
  client = ellmer::chat_anthropic(),
  data_sources = list(reports = commons::data_source(con)),
  semantic_layer = commons::semantic_layer(search_measure),
  instructions = "The reports table holds report metadata only. The text of
    the reports is available only through the search_reports measure: for any
    question about what a report or business unit said, call search_reports
    with call_measure, passing the as_of date from the question."
)

agent$chat(
  "As of 2025-06-30, what did the business units say about the PC refresh?"
)
commons::commons_app(agent)
```

## Conclusion

- Chunk each report's `body`, and attach all of its metadata to every chunk
  with one `mutate()`. Declare the metadata columns up front with
  `extra_cols = reports[0, meta_cols]`.
- From exported files, `yaml12::read_yaml()` gives the metadata and body
  together; convert the dates back to `Date`.
- `embed = NULL` gives a BM25-only store with no embedding model.
- Search with `ragnar_retrieve_bm25()`. Use `conjunctive = TRUE` to know when
  nothing really matched, and `filter` to restrict by date, unit or type.
- Use SQL on the `chunks` table for questions about dates and counts.
- When an LLM uses the store, give it a search tool that enforces `as_of`.
